comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom utilized all $20 billion of authorized stock repurchase amounts (originally authorized in December 2021 and May 2022) prior to their expiration on December 31, 2023. In fiscal year 2024, the company repurchased and retired approximately 67 million shares for $7,176 million.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose their fiscal year 2024 stock repurchase activity, but differ in program status and scale. AMD reported repurchasing 5.9 million shares for $862 million under an ongoing $12 billion program with $4.7 billion remaining, emphasizing the program's indefinite nature. In contrast, Broadcom repurchased 67 million shares for $7,176 million in 2024, which exhausted its prior $20 billion authorized programs that had expired on December 31, 2023, marking a completion of a specific authorization period rather than an open-ended mandate.

sentences.text: The Company has an approved stock repurchase program authorizing repurchases of up to $12 billion of the Company's common stock (Repurchase Program).
During the year ended December 28, 2024, the Company repurchased 5.9 million shares of its common stock under the Repurchase Program for $862 million.
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under this program.
This Repurchase Program does not obligate the Company to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

In December 2021, our Board of Directors authorized a stock repurchase program to repurchase up to $10 billion of our common stock from time to time through December 31, 2022, which was subsequently extended to December 31, 2023.
In May 2022, our Board of Directors authorized another stock repurchase program to repurchase up to an additional $10 billion of our common stock from time to time through December 31, 2023.

During fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022, we repurchased and retired approximately 67 million, 91 million and 117 million shares of our common stock for $7,176 million, $5,824 million and $7,000 million, respectively.
All $20 billion of the authorized amount under these stock repurchase programs was utilized prior to expiration on December 31, 2023.

Micron repurchased 3.2 million shares for $300 million with an aggregate of $7.19 billion already repurchased against a $10 billion limit, indicating significantly higher utilization of its authorization compared to AMD's early-stage execution.

Our Board of Directors has authorized the discretionary repurchase of up to $10 billion of our outstanding common stock through open-market purchases, block trades, privately-negotiated transactions, derivative transactions, and/or pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 trading plans.
We repurchased 3.2 million shares of our common stock for $300 million in 2024 and 8.6 million shares for $425 million in 2023.
Through August 29, 2024, we had repurchased an aggregate of $7.19 billion under the authorization.

comparisons.peer_topic: Share Repurchase Program Authorization and Activity
comparisons.peer_summary: In August 2023, the Board authorized an additional $25.0 billion for share repurchases without expiration, with $9.7 billion spent in fiscal 2024 and $1.9 billion in early 2024. As of January 28, 2024, $22.5 billion remained authorized, and the program aims to offset employee dilution while remaining subject to market conditions.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and NVIDIA both describe active share repurchase programs authorized to offset dilution or return capital, but differ materially in scale and remaining authorization. AMD repurchased 5.9 million shares for $862 million with $4.7 billion remaining. NVIDIA repurchased 21 million shares for $9.7 billion in fiscal 2024 with $22.5 billion remaining authorized, reflecting a much larger capital return program and higher share repurchase volume relative to AMD.
